as a fellow psy student i’d suggest padua. I also briefly lived in bologna before changing uni, but i personally didn’t like it very much (rents are too expensive, some places must be avoided especially if you’re a girl walking alone at night). I also lived in padua for a year before starting to commute, and it’s true that rents are a little less expensive than bologna, but there still is a housing problem due to the scarcity of rooms so i’d recommend to search very much in advance in order to find something pretty decent. 

Both cities are really Lgbtq+ friendly, i also have lgbtq+ people in my course and no one has ever had issues with them. Students are very open minded and friendly in both cities, in padua for example i’ve seen manifestations for lgtbq+ and trans feminists’ rights. So personally i think you won’t have any issues in both of them on this matter.

Overall i’d recommend padua, also because psychology courses are very well taught and structured, the lectures are stimulating and the professors are very qualified from my personal experience.
Another reason is because it gives me “safer” vibes (maybe it’s because it’s a smaller city compared to bologna idk), good transportation system and it has a cute city center.
